paragraphs.source_en: It is impossible, moreover, to control the value of money under inflation. For, as we have seen, the causa-tion is never a merely mechanical one. You cannot, for example, say in advance that a 100 per cent increase in the quantity of money will mean a 50 per cent fall in the value of the monetary unit. The value of money, as we have seen, depends upon the subjective valuations of the people who hold it. And those valuations do not de-pend solely on the quantity of it that each person holds.They depend also on the quality of the money. paragraphs.source_en: In our own day the most persistent argument put for-ward for inflation is that it will “get the wheels of in-dustry turning,” that it will save us from the irretriev-able losses of stagnation and idleness and bring “full employment.” This argument in its cruder form rests on the immemorial confusion between money and real wealth.
